# reconciliation/

Subledger ↔ GL control-account reconciliation, DECOMPOSED into itemised
reconciling items carrying document ids. Read-only. Consumed by the
`reconcile_subledger` MCP tool (`src/lib/mcp/tools/reconcileSubledger.ts`).

## Modules
- `subledgerReconciliationService.ts` — the entry point, `reconcileSubledger(companyId, role, asAtDate)`. Composes the four readers and both bridges.
- `agedReportTotal.ts` — reads the aged report's OWN total from `getARAging` / `getAPAging`. Never recomputes it.
- `unappliedCashService.ts` — cash on a control account not applied to a document, by both mechanisms (a payment row with nothing allocated; control movement with no payment row at all).
- `orphanControlPostings.ts` — the SQL of mechanism 2 (control movement no document claims), before `orphanReversalPairs.ts` drops cancelling pairs.
- `unpostedDocumentService.ts` / `unpostedDocumentQueries.ts` — open documents whose value never reached a control account, split by whether a journal is linked. The service maps; the queries file is the SQL.
- `settlementFlagService.ts` — supplier bills flagged `payment_matched` while still open. An ADVISORY, not a reconciling item.
- `reconcilingItemBuilders.ts` — which bridge an item belongs on. That decision is the substance of the endpoint.
- `unappliedPaymentCash.ts` — mechanism 1 of the unapplied-cash reader: WHICH payments from `shared/unappliedPaymentBasis.ts`, HOW MUCH from their movement on the control account.
- `unappliedCreditNoteService.ts` — approved credit no document has consumed. AP has no credit-note leg in its subledger at all.
- `reconciliationInvariants.ts` — what the reconciliation asserts about its own output. Returned, never thrown.
- `reconcilingWarnings.ts` — `excludedRows` that are deliberately NOT items.
- `reconcilingItemTypes.ts`, `unappliedCashTypes.ts`, `reconciliationMath.ts` — shapes and the two shared arithmetic helpers.

## Caller contract
`reconcileSubledger(companyId, role, asAtDate)`. `role` is a `SubledgerRole`
from `gl/controlAccountService`; only `ar` and `ap` have a document subledger,
and the rest return the GL side with `subledgerTotal: null` and
`subledgerUnavailable` stating why — never a difference of zero. `asAtDate` is a
`'YYYY-MM-DD'` string and stays a string on every path here.

## Business rules
- **TWO BRIDGES, never added together.** `aged_to_subledger` explains why the aged report's total is not the subledger's (open disputes, unallocated credit notes). `subledger_to_control` explains the GL difference. Merging them is why the audit's Brightsphere figure of R1,429,774 reconciled to nothing.
- **Two identities, each with its own residual emitted AS AN ITEM:**
  `controlAccountBalance + Σ(subledger_to_control) = subledgerTotal` and
  `agedTotal + Σ(aged_to_subledger) = subledgerTotal`. `unexplained_difference`
  and `aged_unexplained_difference` are the residuals; a non-zero one is a
  mechanism this code does not yet know about.
- **`agedTotal` is read from the aged report, never recomputed.** Recomputing it hid `unageable_document` claiming a defect #303 had already fixed, worth R12,730,957 of Velocity AR.
- **POINT IN TIME on both sides.** The subledger readers use `shared/agingRewind.ts` — the same rewind the aging reports use, with the same four documented limitations. There is no `afterAsAt`: the readers apply the aging report's `document_date <= as_at` cutoff, so nothing raised after the reporting date is in the subledger at it.
- **EVERY control account, never one — but ONLY accounts carrying the role's SUBTYPE.** There is no canonical AR/AP control account in this schema. `controlAccountAmbiguous` says when more than one account carries the subtype and the balance is their sum. `ar.control.v1` / `ap.control.v1` are deliberately UNOWNED in `contracts/figures.ts`: naming an owner would encode an arbitrary choice as truth.
- **An account is NEVER adopted because documents posted to it.** `settle_by_contra` posts DR Accounts Payable / CR <loan account> through a `supplier_payments` row, so the old posting probe adopted loan accounts as AP control accounts: three "control accounts" on production, a `document_not_on_control_account` item of +R453m and an unexplained difference of −R437m. Those accounts are `postings_on_non_control_accounts` warnings now (`gl/nonControlPostingAccounts.ts`).
- **"Unapplied" has ONE definition** — `shared/unappliedPaymentBasis.ts`, shared with `list_unapplied_receipts` / `list_unapplied_payments`: `total_amount − Σ allocations`, allocations capped at the total, counted when `round2(remainder) > 0`. The reconciler's ITEM amount is still the payment's movement ON THE CONTROL ACCOUNT, because that is what it explains of the difference; the gap between the two is `unapplied_cash_off_control_account` on `excludedRows`, never folded in. Britech on isaflow_dev: 130 receipts worth R7,505,599 by document against an AR control balance of −R329,700.
- **A CANCELLED document does not claim its journal, and does not relieve anything.** Cancelling posts a reversal, so the original and the reversal net to zero on the control account. While the cancelled document still counted as a claimant, only the REVERSAL reached the orphan list — an unbalanced item on a pair that moved nothing: R13,715,088.59 across 322 cancelled payments and R2,871,896.82 across 37 cancelled credit notes on a production copy. Letting the original through lets `dropCancelledReversalPairs` drop both by the outcome rule it already applies.
- **A credit note relieves a document by its ALLOCATION ROWS, never by its journal and never by `applied_amount` through the link column.** The rest is credit no document took up and belongs to `unapplied_credit_note`, which counts it from the other side. Counting the whole journal put it in both places: 12 bills each carrying one applied and one approved note of the same value, R5,740.22 claimed twice. Since migration 677 a note is applied FIFO across several documents, so `applied_amount` is the SUM over all of them and the link column names at most one: reading either attributed a split note wholly to its linked bill and none of it to the rest — −R3,728,724.75 over 150 AP documents against +R3,728,724.79 unexplained on a production copy. `creditNoteRelief.ts` reads the rows, capped at each note's share of what reached the control account, with the pre-677 link column behind a `NOT EXISTS` — the same two-arm shape `shared/agingRewind.ts` uses, so the two reports cannot disagree.
- **Unapplied credit is "NOT draft, NOT cancelled, with a remainder" — never a list of statuses.** `applied` carries a remainder too, because `applyCreditNoteToInvoice` credits `min(total, outstanding)` (mig 529). One such note on isaflow_dev left R230 that neither leg claimed.
- **A REFUND is a payment whose control movement is NEGATIVE.** `DR Bank / CR Accounts Payable` on a `supplier_payments` row. Capping the allocation with a bare `Math.min` picked that negative movement even with nothing allocated, so the item came out at zero and the value became an unnamed residual. The cap is `Math.min(allocated, Math.max(0, movement))`.
- **`item_within_cited_gross` compares Σ|member|, never the group's net.** On a net an overstated member hides behind an opposite-signed one — `posting_with_no_document` netted +R124,704.80 against a cited gross of R686,504.50 with two refund journals in the group. Every item carries `citedAbsAmount` for this.
- **A control-bridge item that nets to exactly zero is not emitted**, because it explains nothing and reads as a finding that resolves itself. Its rows go to `excludedRows` as `net_zero_reconciling_item`: two errors that cancel are still two errors.
- **`posting_with_no_document` is mostly ONE cause class: an allocation journal with no payment document.** Bank allocation posts the control leg and, on some paths, creates no payment row — 39 journals worth R124,704.80 on a production copy, every one stamped `mcp:bulk_allocate_bank_transactions`. The remedy is to create the payment document and apply it.
- **A payment leg is attributed to a document by its ALLOCATED AMOUNT, not by its journal.** Summing the payment journal's control lines per allocation row relieves the document by the WHOLE payment: a R100 receipt with R99.99 applied relieved the invoice by R100 while the unapplied item claimed R0.01 as well, and two allocations from one payment to one invoice doubled it outright.
- **The invariants are returned, not thrown.** `control_plus_items_equals_subledger`, `item_within_cited_gross`, `unexplained_is_the_residual`. A violation is the most interesting thing this endpoint can say about a set of books and a 500 would replace it with nothing. Every item carries `citedGross` so the second one can be checked at all.
- **`gl_accounts.is_active` is never a filter.** It is a picker flag; deactivated accounts hold money.
- **`settlementFlagged` must stay out of `reconcilingItems`.** Its cash is already counted once as `posting_with_no_document`; adding it would drive the residual to minus its amount.
- **A document dated AFTER `as_at` is `settlement_before_document`, never a cut-off finding.** It is not in the subledger at that date, so any shortfall it carries comes from a payment / credit / write-off posted on or before `as_at` and applied to it in advance (a prepayment applied FIFO to a later bill). `document_not_on_control_account` and `document_not_linked_to_journal` now only name documents dated on or before `as_at`. The close gate (`gl/closeReadinessChecks/subLedgerTieCheck.ts`) tolerates `unapplied_receipt`, `unapplied_credit_note` and `settlement_before_document` and fails on everything else on the control bridge — renaming or re-bridging an item type changes what blocks a month-end close.
- **A soft-deleted document's reversal chain is never itemised, at any length.** The sub-ledger side keeps or drops the document by the chain's PARITY as at the date (`shared/softDeleteLedgerPresence`) and `unpostedDocumentService` nets it against its original entry alone, so every link past the original is already in the decomposition. The orphan scan excludes the whole chain (same walk: posted, this tenant, from the document's link), not only the entry `soft_delete_journal_reversals` records — that row does not move when the delete reversal is itself reversed by hand.
- A row's contribution to `unpostedDocumentService` must be the SAME number the subledger snapshot counted for it — same status rule, same cutoff, same rewind. Drift between the two definitions lands in the residual and reads as a finding about the books.

## Recent changes
- 2026-10-02 (D7): a hand-reversed delete reversal no longer fails the AR/AP close checks. Mechanism 2 excluded only the `soft_delete_journal_reversals` entry R, so once R was reversed by hand R2 had no partner and was itemised as `posting_with_no_document` with an equal and opposite `unexplained_difference` on books that tied (first bad: ccd44bba3, when the close checks began reading the itemisation). It now excludes the deleted document's whole reversal chain; this also stops itemising a journal hand-reversed BEFORE its document was deleted. A live document's hand reversal is still itemised. Query moved to `orphanControlPostings.ts` for the 300-line rule. Tests: `tests/integration/k053-deleted-document-chain-reconciliation.int.test.ts`, `k053-aging-as-at-reversal-date.int.test.ts`; the L3 fixture's stray cent now rides on a draft credit note, since a forged sdjr row no longer excludes anything.
- 2026-09-30 (close-gate as-at): `buildControlBridgeItems` takes `asAtDate` and splits documents dated after it into a new `settlement_before_document` item (prepayments applied to later documents). On Velocity Fibre every one of 700 `document_not_on_control_account` items across 32 month-ends (May 2025 – Aug 2026, up to R5.2m a month) was this and none was a real cut-off error. The AR / AP close gates now read `reconcileSubledger` and tolerate the item. Tests: `tests/unit/mcp/w2/subledgerReconciliation.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/gl/subLedgerTieCheck.test.ts`.
- 2026-09-19 (supplier refunds): a refund journal leaves `posting_with_no_document`. A supplier refund's DR Bank / CR Accounts Payable entry had no document to claim it, so it was counted here as a posting nothing owned. It now carries a `supplier_payments` row with a NEGATIVE `total_amount` (migration 681), which `shared/unappliedPaymentBasis` reports as a negative remainder and `unappliedPaymentCash` turns into a signed reconciling item. **The zero floor in `unappliedPaymentCash` was already written for this shape** — it caps the ALLOCATED figure, never the movement — so the item is the control movement itself, signed the way it moved the account, and the identity still holds. The one shape that cannot be documented is a deposit allocated straight to the AP control account: it credits the payable without naming a supplier, so the backfill reports it under `refund_on_control_unresolved` and mints nothing. One line on production, R120,290.00.
- 2026-09-19 (credit-note allocations): the document scan reads `credit_note_allocations` instead of `credit_notes.applied_amount` through the single link column, so a note applied FIFO over several documents relieves each of them by its own row. New `creditNoteRelief.ts` holds both arms and the proportional cap. On `isaflow_staging` AP for 4a159669 went from `document_not_on_control_account` −R3,728,724.75 (150 docs) against +R3,728,724.79 unexplained, to +R0.04 (4 docs) against R0.00, all three invariants holding; AR unchanged at R0.00. Pinned by `tests/integration/l3b-credit-note-allocations.int.test.ts` (service-driven shapes) and `l3c-credit-note-relief-caps.int.test.ts` (the proportional cap, the zero floor, the cancelled-with-rows guard and the as-at bound, each on a forged shape and each proved by mutation). The relief is dated by the note's `credit_date`, matching `agingRewind`, with the control-side cap still bounded by the journal's `entry_date`; dating it by the journal alone relieved the control side of a note the subledger had just rewound. The same commit fixed the L3 fixture, whose credit notes were auto-applying FIFO into bills other cases assert are open: on a faithful master checkout that left the AP residual at +R229.99 where the fixture builds −R0.01. (The fixture-repair commit message says R1,150.00; that came from an earlier run of the same check and did not reproduce. R229.99 is the figure a clean master reproduces.)
- 2026-09-18 (L3 round 2): measured against a full production copy (`isaflow_staging`). Three mis-detections found and fixed — cancelled documents still claiming their journals, credit notes relieving a document by their journal rather than their applied amount, and unapplied credit read off a status list. AP went from an unexplained R15,707,991.88 to R0.00, with `posting_with_no_document` falling from −R16,462,280.61 to +R124,704.80 and `document_not_on_control_account` from +R878,993.57 to +R0.04.
- 2026-09-18 (L3): control accounts resolved by SUBTYPE ONLY (the posting probe is gone); one shared definition of an unapplied payment; `unapplied_credit_note` itemised (AP's subledger carries no credit notes, so supplier credit fell into the residual unnamed); payment legs attributed by allocated amount; invariants reported. Verified on isaflow_dev: residual 0.00 on every AR and AP company, all three invariants holding, 144 previously-silent off-control payments named.

## Testing
`tests/unit/mcp/w2/`. The unit suites mock `sql`, so they cannot see whether a
statement Postgres would accept was built — every table read here also has a
DB-gated test (`*.integration.test.ts`) that runs it inside
`BEGIN … ROLLBACK` against `isaflow_dev`.
